name: Hashcat
what: A high-performance password recovery engine that runs on GPUs and CPUs. It cracks many hash formats (NTLM, NetNTLMv2, Kerberos, bcrypt and hundreds more) using dictionaries, rules, masks and hybrid attacks.
when: Offline, on hardware you control, to measure password strength of hashes obtained during an authorized assessment or from your own password audit exports.
example: Download the release from hashcat.net or build from the GitHub repository on a dedicated cracking box.
Identify the hash mode (`hashcat --help` / example hashes) for example NetNTLMv2 from Responder.
Run a dictionary attack against an approved hash file: `hashcat -m 5600 hashes.txt rockyou.txt -r rules/best64.rule`.
Report crack rates and weak patterns to the client; never reuse cracked production passwords outside the engagement vault.
pitfalls: Cracking must stay offline; do not attack live authentication endpoints.
GPU drivers and OpenCL/CUDA setup dominate install time; test on a lab hash first.
Storing cracked plaintext next to production identity data is a serious handling risk; encrypt and wipe on schedule.
